new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary word stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the (inflected) word regardless of syllable shape; certain postposed elements (=ga topic, =da accusative, =mi affirmative, -lla 'just', =chu Y/N) are optionally outside the stress domain, so stress may appear antepenultimate on the surface string when they are not cliticized.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress on every second syllable to the left of the primary stress (p. 55, ex. 92 /ˌtawga riGˌsiSka-ˈguna/); apparent secondary stress to the right of primary before =ma is analysed as phrasal.
new_statements.exceptions: (i) Postposed =ga, =da, =mi, -lla optionally cliticize: ['wataza] ~ [wa'taza] 'just a year' (sec. 5.2, pp. 51-52); (ii) a focused element in yes-no questions takes primary stress on its LAST syllable, overriding penultimate stress (pp. 52-53); (iii) contractions often keep stress on the syllable it would have had without contraction, yielding surface final stress, though penultimate is also possible (p. 53, exx. 86-87); (iv) =ma 'certainly' behaves as a separate word for stress (pp. 54-56).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word including inflectional suffixes; some enclitics optionally excluded. Final stress is a phrase-level focus device in yes-no questions. Data are the author's SIL fieldwork in Salasaca, Tungurahua.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Salasaca Quichua (SQ), spoken in Salasaca parish, Tungurahua province, Ecuador — the variety Glottolog No dialect mismatch.

sources.note: Ch. 5 'Stress' (pp. 49-56): stress in SQ is most commonly penultimate; inflected verbs and nouns always penultimate; postposed =ga, =da, =mi, -lla (and =chu) optionally cliticize so stress may fall as if they were outside the word; focused element in yes-no questions gets final primary stress; contractions may keep stress on original syllable; secondary stress on every second syllable to the left of primary; =ma treated as separate word on stress evidence.
